topic: SpaceX's rocket booster has no landing legs -- it gets caught by a tower instead
title: The Rocket With Zero Landing Legs — Watch How SpaceX Actually Lands It
description: AI-narrated commentary: SpaceX's biggest rocket booster doesn't land on legs at all -- it gets caught out of the sky by a giant tower. Here's the actual engineering reason why.

hook_candidates.text: SpaceX's biggest rocket booster has zero landing legs — two giant metal arms catch it out of the sky instead.
Why would you build a 20-story rocket booster with no landing legs at all?
Landing legs aren't what makes a rocket reusable — SpaceX proved that by removing them completely.
In 2024, a robotic tower reached out and caught a falling rocket in midair — on the very first attempt.

payoff_mechanism: Landing legs are dead weight a booster has to carry to space and back for one three-second touchdown, so removing them frees up mass for extra fuel, and the tower's arms can catch it directly and prepare it to fly again within hours.
share_trigger: Send this to the friend who insists rockets need legs like the moonlander, captioned: 'they don't anymore, look at this.'

beats.text: Zero **landing legs.** That's how SpaceX's biggest rocket booster comes home.
Instead, a giant tower reaches out and catches it **in midair**.
Losing the legs means **more fuel** — ready to fly again within hours. Follow for the next one.
